questions.q: What is the author's main point?
options: Heavy AI use quickly erodes persistence and independent thinking
ChatGPT gives unreliable math answers that mislead students
Smartphones damage thinking faster than chatbots ever could
AI assistance improves persistence once the chatbot is gone
questions.explain: He argues AI help degrades cognitive fitness fast, though the effects may not be permanent.

questions.q: What task did participants in the experiment do?
options: Summarize long newspaper articles aloud
Write short essays about their personal goals
Debug short programs written in Python
Solve math problems involving fractions
questions.explain: They solved a series of math problems involving fractions, with one group using ChatGPT.

questions.q: What happened when the chatbot was turned off?
options: AI group accuracy fell below control and many skipped questions
The control group's accuracy fell and many of them quit early
The AI group kept outperforming the control group on every problem
Both groups performed equally well and finished every question
questions.explain: The AI group's accuracy fell below the control group and many gave up and skipped questions.

questions.q: What does the author say is new about these findings?
options: That the effects are permanent
The existence of cognitive harm
That math is affected
The jaw-dropping speed of the effects
questions.explain: He says the new element is how fast the impacts appear, unlike smartphone trends.

questions.q: What does the author imply about whether these effects are permanent?
options: They are surely permanent after even brief chatbot exposure
They have been disproven by follow-up studies of participants
Unknown; they might improve if retested without AI help
They affect only younger users who grew up with smartphones
questions.explain: He says we don't yet know if effects are permanent, and participants might do better later.
